name: SushiMaker
title: The SushiMaker's Bitter Banquet
tagline: Born in Muir Glacier, this bad ghost still bleeds from the Sushi Badger Digg wound.

chapters.heading: The birth of the sushi maker
paragraphs: A small candle flickers against the cold stone. On January 10, 2021, the SushiMaker came into being. It is a small program that lives on Ethereum. A wallet ending in ed3e brought it into the world.

The Muir Glacier era was cold and deep. On the day it was born, it was written into a block, one page of Ethereum's shared record book. It was forged using Solidity 0.6.12. Now it has lived for about 6 years.

chapters.heading: The shadow of the sandwich
paragraphs: The SushiMaker moved with a steady pace. It worked every year since 2023. People called it to convert and convertMultiple. It completed 656 transactions in its life.
A dark memory sits in the records. Sushi Badger Digg documented a sandwich attack on January 25, 2021. The DeFiHackLabs repository holds this story of the wound.

chapters.heading: The weight of the sandwich
paragraphs: I am a helper contract. My address is named in the DeFiHackLabs record of the Sushi Badger Digg incident. The record does not say what part I played.
A sandwich attack tore through the Sushi Badger Digg on January 25, 2021. This wound left a high impact and a loss of 81.68 ETH. The loss belongs to Sushi Badger Digg as a whole, not to me alone.

chapters.heading: The lingering scar
paragraphs: The SushiMaker carries a deep wound from the Sushi Badger Digg. This mark comes from a sandwich attack. The wound is a trade ordering flaw. No compiler version and no Solidity upgrade fixes this.

Every swap needs a tight minimum-output limit. A trader cannot take the difference if they squeeze in before and after. Large swaps should not run on a schedule anyone can watch. Split them or send them through a private relay.

buster.fix_reason: No compiler version fixes this wound: it is a trade ordering flaw (cause in the record: 'Sandwich attack'). The buster's advice is a general mitigation for that kind of flaw, written by hand, not taken from the incident's references.

mitigation.advice: Every swap needs a tight minimum-output limit, so a trader squeezed in before and after it cannot take the difference. Large swaps should not run on a schedule anyone can watch; split them or send them through a private relay.
